Title: On the role of finance in greening Moroccan real estate assets
text: CONFERENCE ON THE ROLE OF FINANCE IN GREENING MOROCCAN REAL ESTATE ASSETS GREEN FINANCE IN MOROCCO: COMMITMENTS, ACHIEVEMENTS AND AMBITIONS Address by Mr. Abdellatif Jouahri Governor of Bank Al-Maghrib Rabat, May 11, 2017 President of the Economic, Social and Environmental Council, Chairman of the COP22 Scientific Committee President of the Casablanca-Settat Region, Secretary General of the Ministry of Energy, Mining and Sustainable Development, Distinguished Presidents, Ladies and gentlemen, It is my great pleasure to join this green finance conference, which offers me a new opportunity to express the will and determination of the Moroccan financial community to accompany our countryd5s efforts in line with the global climate change agenda. This event is, for me, a contribution in implementing the commitments laid out in the financial system roadmap with regard to a major sector, namely real estate. I would like to thank Mr. Abdellatif Zaghnoun and his team for this initiative, which aims to keep up the COP22 momentum. After the historic agreements of the COP21, the world is now totally mobilized to start the implementation phase, launched at the COP22 in Marrakesh last November. Hence, just as like 2016 was one of the worst years in terms of climate change manifestations, with a record temperature, it is the year when the international community confirmed its determination to act, with Morocco playing a major active role. Let me first address some international developments and initiatives before returning to the specific case of our country. Ladies and gentlemen, Signs of the green finance development around the world are increasingly visible in all components of the financial system. In the securities market, green bond issues have recorded an exponential growth. Although they represent less than 1 percent of total bond issues, their volume in 2016 is seven times higher than three years ago. China, one of the biggest polluters, but also one of the most active in this field, accounts alone for almost 27 percent of such issues. It is worth reminding here that Bank Al-Maghrib has invested USD 100 million in World Bank green bonds. At the stock market, initiatives are multiplying to promote green investment. Among these is the Sustainable Stock Exchanges (SSE) initiative organized by UNCTAD, UNEP and other UN global networks. The aim of such initiative is to encourage green bonds listing and publication of green stock indexes to serve as indicators for investors wishing to reduce their investmentsd5 carbon footprint. Today, more than sixty stock exchanges, including that of Casablanca, have adhered to this initiative all over the world. The banking system represents, as you know, the most important source of financing for the economy, particularly in emerging and developing countries. As such, it could have a definite influence on the behavior of economic units and their attitudes towards the environment, particularly those involved in the real estate sector. The latter, according to the World Bank, contributes 40 percent to global CO2 emissions and more than one third to greenhouse gas emissions. Therefore, the greening of this sector may play a significant role in fighting climate change, hence the importance of the debates projected during the second round table on this subject. Numerous initiatives were taken in support of the banking sectord5s contribution to green finance development. Several new products have been launched to encourage preferential c7green lending. For instance, banks in Canada and Australia have set advantageous rates for the purchase of vehicles with low CO2 emissions. Also, some countries, such as the United Kingdom, have gone so far as to create green public investment banks to support low-carbon infrastructures and environment-friendly projects such as water and waste management. At a more global level, and back in 2003, the International Finance Corporation has established the d2Equator Principlesd3 which provide financial institutions with a framework to determine, assess and manage environmental and social risks. To date, nearly 90 financial institutions from 37 countries, both advanced and emerging, including a Moroccan bank, have adhered to these principles. These efforts are clearly driven and supported by central banks and banking sector supervisory authorities, some of which have established guidelines to ensure, inter alia, that social and environmental priorities are taken into account in loan-granting decisions. However, banking institutions are somehow reluctant to meet additional requirements related to environment protection. Such situation is partly understandable considering that these institutions continue to suffer from the aftermath of one of the worst global financial crises, and from tighter prudential regulations, which makes such environmental considerations sound like a source of additional difficulties. Ladies and gentlemen, Let me now go back to the case of Morocco. Sustainability and environment protection are a priority issue at the highest level of the state. Our vision of development, as reflected in HM the Kingd5s speeches, is centered on two pillars, human and sustainable development. In fact, the study d2Global wealth and Intangible Capital of Moroccod3, carried out by the EESC and BAM upon royal instructions, highlights the willingness to introduce the criteria of intangible capital sustainability and development in public policiesd5 development and monitoring. The energy strategy is a concrete example of such orientation. Our country is today cited as an example of energy transition and renewable energies development, expected to meet 52 percent of the countryd5s needs by 2030. The financial system, in view of its role in mobilizing necessary resources for financing sustainable development, can only be at the core of the national mobilization against climate change. Today, Moroccan banks are already involved in programs of financing renewable energy development. Some have developed specific products to support companies engaged in a sustainable development process, while others have taken the initiative to create investment funds dedicated to companies which are socially responsible or engaged in energy efficiency processes. In order to strengthen and coordinate the various initiatives and therefore trigger the necessary synergies, the Ministry of Finance, Bank Al-Maghrib and the various stakeholders concerned have developed a roadmap for greening the Moroccan financial sector. This map sets up the actions enabling the different components of the sector to contribute to fulfilling our countryd5s commitments with regard to sustainable development and to the fight against climate change. Let me remind you of the main strands of this initiative which I was asked to present at the COP22 in Marrakech. In the first place, banks commit to incorporate the environmental dimension in their loan- granting or investment process, namely by setting up a system for environmental risks management and impact-assessment. The second part concerns developing green savings products both for banks and insurance companies, creating specialized investment vehicles and promoting green bonds issuance. The central bank will consider, when necessary, establishing a refinancing mechanism for green projects, similar to the one set up for VSMEs. The third pillar concerns promoting financial inclusion, by implementing a national financial inclusion strategy, and developing a low-cost mobile national payment solution. The other areas focus on capacity development and improved transparency and market discipline. Stakeholders pledge to raise awareness and educate economic operators on environmental concerns. Ladies and gentlemen, This roadmap is not an end in itself; it is rather the start of a long path that we have just begun. We are all aware that it is easier to develop a vision than to implement it. For this reason, we have entrusted to the Coordination Committee, which brings together regulators and financial sector authorities, with the task of regularly monitoring the commitments made under this roadmap. Its mission is to draw up progress reports on the achievements made, identify the difficulties faced and make the necessary adjustments. We will also communicate about our achievements and progress to federate, further mobilize and strengthen the virtuous synergies. In the same vein, we took the initiative, on the occasion of the COP22 and in collaboration with the United Nations Environment Program, to bring together central banks of Northern and Southern countries to discuss sustainable financing. However, this meeting could not be held due to some timetable constraints, but we never despaired to hold it, although we noticed that some central banks in advanced countries are rather reluctant. Ladies and gentlemen, At Bank Al-Maghrib, we are well aware that our credibility in promoting sustainability depends on our own practices as a company. That is why our methods and work processes within the Bank are guided by this requirement, and are, as such, certified according to the relevant standards, particularly the Environmental Management and the Occupational Health & Safety Management Repository. In addition, in 2016, we started publishing our Corporate Social Responsibility Report. In recognition of all these efforts, Bank Al-Maghrib was invited to join IFCd5s Sustainable Banking Network, created in 2012 to help regulatory authorities of emerging countries develop d2responsible lendingd3 policies and guidelines for environmental and social risks management. Ladies and gentlemen, The global fight against climate change cannot achieve tangible results without a collective mobilization and a comprehensive response. In fact, besides financial actors, public authorities, companies, civil society, the media and citizens all have their share of responsibility in this action. Finance is not the only sector which requires greening; the latter should also cover public policy, namely government spending, supply policy, taxation, and so on. For their part, companies also are urged to meet the environmental requirements in their choices of investment, supply, management and operation. Civil society and the media also have a significant role to play, namely informing, educating and sensitizing citizens and businesses about climate change issues and putting pressure on decision-making centers. Finally, citizens are encouraged to consume green and to minimize the environmental impact of their consumption and their activities. All together, we can move ahead in our fight against climate change which secures our future and that of the coming generations. It is certainly a long-term and time-consuming project. Thank you for your attention and I wish you every success.

Title: At the Conference on "Monetary and financial decolonization in Africa in the 20th century"
text: Conference on "Money in Africa - Monetary and Financial Decolonization in Africa in the 20th Century" Round table Monetary policy in Africa today: between the sovereignty and international cooperation Speech by Mr. Abdellatif Jouahri Wali de Bank Al-Maghrib Banco de Portugal, 10 October 2017 Governors, dear friends, Ladies and gentlemen First of all, I would like to inform the organisers of the choice of the theme, especially since these are issues that we rarely have the opportunity to address in the financial and monetary fields. The pleasure is all the greater for me that I keep a very good memory of these beautiful buildings where I had the opportunity, at the invitation of my friend Governor Carlos Da Silva Costa four years ago, to give a conference on economic and social changes in Morocco. It is also a pleasure for me to meet Mr. Olivier Feiertag who accompanied us for the elaboration of a book on the history of the Central Bank of Morocco. On monetary decolonization, I would first like to begin by pointing out that monetary sovereignty in Morocco has been a reality for a very long time. Indeed, already in the 8th century, under the reign of the first dynasty, Morocco began to mint its own currency, the dirham. The latter was replaced by other symbols by some subsequent dynasties before it was adopted again during the reign of the Alawites until 1920 when the protectorate French - which began in 1912 - introduced the Moroccan franc. In the aftermath of the indppendance, the Moroccan authorities began a process of monetary and economic decolonization. One of the first actions in this context was the creation in June 1959 of the Banque du Maroc to replace the former colonial pmission bank, which had existed since 1907. On October 17 of the same year, the Moroccan dirham was again adopted as the official currency of the country as a substitute for the Moroccan franc. It may be considered that monetary decolonization stricto sensu, or what Mr Feiertag called "moroccoexit", was completed that day, but in reality it was only the beginning of a long learning process that lasted until the beginning of the 1980s. It was, in particular, the "Moroccanization" of the financial system and the gradual replacement of foreign executives by nationals. I myself am part of this first generation of executives of the Bank of Morocco who have been called upon to take over the national financial system. A new consecration of this monetary sovereignty was the creation in 1987 of Dar As-Sikkah to provide Morocco with its own factory for the manufacture of banknotes and coins. I think it's been a great success, especially since we are responding to the needs of other countries and we have developed first-rate partnerships. I would like here, in the presence of my African friends, to recall the wish of the late His Majesty Hassan II expressed during his inaugural speech: "Let heaven heaven may this institute grow and prosper, not only for itself, but also for the countries of the region and I think above all of our great African family ... . In the same year, and to further reaffirm the national identity of the Central Bank, the name Bank of Morocco was replaced by Bank Al-Maghrib. Everything I have just said corresponds to a narrow vision of the concept, limiting it to the establishment of a currency and the institution of a monetary authority specific to the country. It does not include in particular the notion of decision-making sovereignty and the autonomy of monetary policy, which, as you know, also depends on both the nature of the exchange rate regime and the level of opening of the capital account. We, too, in this area, like many countries, opted for a fixed exchange rate regime after the creation of our own currency. Initially, the value of the dirham was linked to that of the French franc, but with the diversification of trading partners, it was anchored to a basket of currencies whose composition was adjusted several times to take into account the pvolution of the country's trade structure. Today, this basket is composed of 60% of the euro and 40% of the US dollar. With regard to the capital account, Morocco has opted for a gradual opening, resulting today in a total convertibility of the dirham for non-residents and partial for residents. It can therefore be concluded, with reference to Mundell's famous triangle of incompatibility, that monetary policy in a fixed regime has partial autonomy. In the early 80s, many developing countries found themselves facing budgetary impasses that led them to resort to international donors, including the IMF and the World Bank. The latter have made their financial support conditionality subject to sometimes binding conditionality, leaving little room for manoeuvre on the part of the national authorities. Why did we get to this point? Clearly, this has been the result of an ambition sometimes to accelerate the development process, leading to an unsustainable pace of public spending, including investment. It has been exacerbated by significant fluctuations in the prices of raw materials, particularly oil, and the rise in interest rates on the financial markets. The outbreak of the ensuing debt crisis was a harsh awakening and highlighted the importance of ensuring the sustainability of macroeconomic balances, to which no special attention was being paid at the time. That being said, and despite the difficulties of negotiations with the donors - because in front of them, we only had very reduites.je do not believe that we can speak of "recolonization". By way of illustration, among the measures recommended by the IMF and the World Bank as part of an adjustment program was the devaluation of the dirham, which both institutions considered overvalued. The aim was to improve export competitiveness and improve the external accounts situation. It should be remembered that at the time, the IMF and the World Bank presented "solution menus" and not "a la carte solutions". The authorities ended up, despite some reluctance, agreeing to initiate a process of gradual adjustment of the value of the dirham. When I myself returned to Bank Al-Maghrib in 2003, I felt that it was necessary to take stock of at least the impact of the PAS. But without waiting for the results, we can at least conclude that on the social level it was relatively heavy. Now if we look at "the full half of the glass", we can certainly say that the IMF's "conditionality" was binding, but we cannot deny either that it helped to initiate a dynamic of reforms. In this respect, I will briefly refer to the process of liberalization of the financial system in my country. Since 1988, Morocco has accelerated reforms in the field of foreign exchange regulations. Since 1993, current transactions have become completely free and the capital account fully open for non-residents. With regard to the banking sector, with the adoption of the Banking Act of 1993, it has been the subject of significant deregulation, including the introduction of new regulatory and supervisory instruments. Similarly, the conduct of monetary policy has been marked by the gradual use of indirect intervention instruments. The crpdit's framework policies as well as the compulsory jobs of the banks have been gradually abandoned and all interest rates have since 1996 been determined by the market (and no longer set administratively). Thanks to these and other efforts, Morocco has been able to establish its macroeconomic balances, continue its reforms according to economic and financial developments and - since 1993 - make the dirham convertible for current operations. Thus, after a first redesign in 2006 that assigned to the bank The preparation of price stability is one of its main tasks and has endowed it with a wide range of interest and new statutes. after the 2008 crisis, they are being adopted, further strengthening its independence and broadening its missions, particularly to include financial stability. All the time, with the choice of openness it has made, Morocco has signed 56 Free Trade Agreements and has turned to Africa politically, economically and financially. With the ambition to priger Casablanca as a financial hub .currently ranked by the Global Financial Centres Index first in Africa and 3rd for the MENA region. Turning towards Africa, Morocco is apprring, after a few years of preparation, to take a new step by starting a gradual flexibilization of its exchange rate regime and a migration to a framework of inflation targeting. The principle of structural adjustment certainly represents a difficult episode in the history of Morocco and probably many developing countries, but I think, nevertheless, that we have learned useful lessons from it. These include the need to maintain the momentum of reforms and to ensure the preservation of macroeconomic balances, which are better bulwarks against threats to sovereignty. International monetary cooperation could play an important role in compensating at least partially for the loss of State sovereignty that has resulted from these developments. It must be said that economic globalization and the increasing intpgration of financial markets mean that the concept of monetary sovereignty in the strict sense is largely "undermined" in the face of a reality marked by increasingly large and volatile capital flows. The most illustrative aspect in this respect would be the impact of monetary policy decisions in the United States on other countries, both well advanced and prosperous. Market expectations related to the US Federal Reserve's policy decisions increase the volatility of capital flows, thus inducing strong pressure on their currencies, and destabilize their macroeconomic balances. As a result, open economies find themselves hostage to the financial cycles of advanced economies and face the constraints of what some economists, including IMF research director Maurice Obstfeld, call the triangle of financial incompatibility. The latter, less known and differing from Mundell's incompatibility triangle, states that macro-prudential policy cannot be effective when capital flows are free. Returning to Africa, in reality we are more impacted through other channels, such as commodity prices or financing conditions on the international market. We can also broaden the debate on sovereignty to, in particular, what awaits us under the digital revolution and its implications, particularly the development of virtual currencies and the rise of large multinationals that control data such as the famous GAFA, put strong pressure on the authorities and even risk challenging their sovereignty in several areas. International cooperation would make it possible to meet these challenges. Moreover, in some forums, such as the International Monetary and Financial Committee, the G20 or the Group of 24, the major economies are often called upon to consider the impact of their decisions on other countries. This cooperation, especially African, must be believed! Africa must belong to Africans. Morocco's African orientation in recent years is precisely in line with this logic. It is essentially based on the development of mutually beneficial joint projects in several areas. -In particular, we have concluded agreements and conventions with several central banks of the continent such as the BCEAO, the BEAC, the Central Bank of the Republic of Guinea, the Central Bank of Tunisia, the Central Bank of Mauritania or the Central Bank of Djibouti. -On the economic level, Morocco plans to integrate the ECOWAS zone. -On the financial front, we have pushed our operators and our banking system into a win-win approach for the benefit of the people of the host countries as well. In the end, we must remain vigilant to implement the necessary reforms - even painful - at the right time to face the various shocks and this from the first signs.

Ladies and Gentlemen, The last decade has seen profound changes linked to the development of information technologies and the Internet, which have fostered the creation of new Web services that affect all aspects of current economic and financial activity, thus creating huge amounts of data: "Big Data". Abuses such as the "Facebook Cambridge Analytica" scandal, or that of the American Credit Bureau "Equifax" are some examples. This has made it necessary and even crucial to adapt the regulatory framework governing this 'new industry'. The GDPR, which entered into force in May 2018, strives to strike a balance between the development of digital technology and the protection of people's fundamental rights. This new European regulation applies to any organization, which processes personal data, as long as it is established on the territory of the European Union or its activity directly targets European residents. Thanks to the efforts of the banking community, under the aegis of the CNDP and Bank-Al Maghrib, the national banking sector has successfully brought it into compliance with the provisions of Law No. 09-08. Internally, Bank Al-Maghrib was the first public and financial institution to implement a compliance management system with personal data protection requirements in 2012. The Bank's efforts continue to align with this new regulatory framework by putting into perspective two key words "Compliance" and "Exemplarity". The various panels as rich as diversified planned in the program will make it possible to cover all the dimensions related to our theme, so I have no doubt about the success of your work. text: NATIONAL AWARENESS CAMPAIGN UNDER THE THEME "The prevention of money laundering, a guarantee for a healthy economy  SPEECH BY MR. ABDELLATIF JOUAHRI GOVERNOR OF BANK AL-MAGHRIB INAUGURAL SESSION Rabat Wednesday, October 31, 2007 Mr. Speaker of the House of Representatives, Dear Ministers, Dear Chairmen of the Parliamentary Committees, Ambassadors and members of the diplomatic corps accredited in Rabat, The Attorneys General of the King, the Prosecutors and the Magistrates Representatives of Regional Institutions and International Dear Presidents and Chief Executive Officers, Dear Presidents of Professional Associations, Ladies and gentlemen It is an honor and a real pleasure for me to welcome you today to the Bank Al-Maghrib Training Center for the launch of the national awareness campaign under the theme "Prevention of money laundering, a guarantee for a healthy economy", which will span nearly four months and cover all regions of the Kingdom. Allow me at the outset to welcome and express my deepest thanks to all the personalities who have kindly responded to our invitation and honoured us with their presence at this inaugural meeting, despite their many commitments, thus demonstrating their particular interest in the object and aims of this campaign. Organized jointly by the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Economy and Finance and Bank Al-Maghrib, this campaign comes a few months after the entry into force of Law No. 43-05 on the fight against money laundering, to respond to the insistent request made by parliamentary groups and committees on the occasion of the examination and adoption of the draft law in question. It responds to a large extent to the concerns of the legislator and sets as its main objectives to clarify the aims, content and scope of the new legal framework and to adopt a common approach in its interpretation and application. Similarly, this campaign aims to raise awareness among the various actors concerned of the importance of the preventive approach in this area and the establishment of communication mechanisms between the supervisory and supervisory authorities and the parties subject to the obligation as part of a regular consultation process. I would like to point out, first of all, that the legislator has ensured that the legal anti-money laundering system is adapted to the national context and accompanied by all the guarantees in terms of preserving professional secrecy and protecting the persons subject to it against any legal proceedings arising from the performance of their obligations. This mechanism, which is also part of the Kingdom's participation in the mobilization of the international community in the fight against organized financial crime, incorporates into domestic law the international commitments made by our country under the bilateral and multilateral conventions it has ratified, the recommendations of the FATF and the Basel Committee on the duty of vigilance towards customers as well as the relevant provisions of the Security Council resolutions, based on Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations, which form one of the pillars of the international legal order in the field of the fight against terrorism. The fight against financial crime has also become an essential component in cooperation agreements with our foreign partners, in particular in the framework of cooperation and free trade agreements concluded with several countries. The compliance of the national system with international standards in the fight against money laundering and the financing of terrorism is assessed, according to a uniform methodology applied to all countries, by the Counter-Terrorism Committee of the United Nations Security Council and the Financial Action Task Force for the Middle East and North Africa, constituted in 2004 and of which the Kingdom of Morocco is one of the founding States. This assessment is an essential element in the assessment, made by the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, of economic and financial stability and therefore influences the rating assigned to Morocco by the specialized agencies. In view of all these elements, it appears that consultation on the issue of combating money laundering and the financing of terrorism is of paramount importance for the improvement of the business environment in our country, given the vital role that can be played in preventing our economic and financial system from being used for illicit purposes. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN It is now established that money laundering has a highly negative effect on a nation's economy and social well-being. It alters inter-company relations, increases the risks of financial institutions, undermines the conduct of economic and financial policy and seriously damages the country's reputation, making it vulnerable to the development of criminal activities. This form of crime is all the more insidious because it often uses front companies that ingeniously inject the proceeds of criminal activities into lawful channels, to hide their true origin. In addition, money laundering promotes, on the one hand, low-quality investments, speculative activities and capital volatility and, on the other hand, strengthens the financial power of criminals, in an international environment marked by the globalization of the economy and the transnational nature of criminal activities that borrow constantly mutating forms in increasingly financialized economies. For my part, I would like to focus in particular on the domestic banking and financial sector, which is directly under the supervision and control of Bank Al-Maghrib, in order to stress that the integrity of this sector requires compliance with rigorous legal, professional and ethical standards and the strengthening of confidence in banking and financial institutions and the preservation of their image and reputation. Three major issues seem to me to have to be identified by these institutions: - a cultural challenge of raising awareness, training and mobilizing their human resources so that they appropriate the new devices and modes of behavior they call for; - a technical challenge dictated by the adaptation of information systems and the segmentation of customers according to risks; - an efficiency issue linked to the requirement for a reinforced and reliable reporting system. Thus, Bank Al-Maghrib, as part of the exercise of its statutory missions, anticipated the entry into force of the anti-money laundering law, initiating, in collaboration with professional organizations, actions aimed, in particular, at strengthening prudential measures, establishing and disseminating a true culture of vigilance, prevention, compliance and ethics. In this regard, Bank Al-Maghrib has, since December 2003, set the minimum rules that credit institutions are required to observe as part of the duty of vigilance with regard to customers. That duty of vigilance was subsequently enshrined in Article 84 of the new Banking Law, promulgated on 14 February 2006 and extended to any transaction the economic cause or lawfulness of which is not apparent. The provisions of the Banking Act as well as those of the Anti-Money Laundering Act led Bank Al-Maghrib to supplement and update, in August 2007, the circular on the vigilance system of 24 December 2003, by providing for rules on customer profiling according to the degree of risk, the setting of thresholds above which transactions could be considered unusual or suspicious and the special examination of certain financial transactions carried out by professional intermediaries. The scope of this circular has been extended to bodies treated as credit institutions. Therefore, we have demanded that these institutions set up a structure dedicated to the management of the internal vigilance system to ensure liaison with the Financial Intelligence Processing Unit, placed with the Prime Minister, and have a centralized, adequate and efficient information system. The effectiveness of all these measures necessarily calls for the establishment, on the one hand, of training and awareness programs for the staff of the subject organizations and, on the other hand, of the compliance function. We have thus supplemented this vigilance system with two directives dated 31 August 2007. The first sets out the principles for credit institutions to establish the compliance function, in charge of preventing the risk of judicial, administrative or disciplinary sanctions, financial loss or damage to reputation following non-compliance with legal and regulatory provisions, and ethical and professional standards and practices specific to their activity. The second, relating to governance within credit institutions, consists of a reference framework of sound practices for the implementation by these institutions of an efficient mode of governance. These measures have made it possible to prepare the banking system well for the implementation of the anti-money laundering law, as can be seen from the Central Bank's assessment of banks' internal arrangements. The initial results of this evaluation are generally satisfactory. Banks have established the compliance function, appointed its managers and their alternates, implemented configurable software packages adapted to the handling of suspicious transactions and customer profiling and have equipped themselves with means of analysis and detection in order to assume their obligation to report suspicions to the Financial Intelligence Processing Unit. Of course, it is imperative that these devices are constantly adapted and regularly monitored. Bank Al-Maghrib, as a taxable person, has itself complied with the new legal requirements, by adopting an institutional, operational and technical system in accordance with the best practices of the Central Banks in this area. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN The improvement of the rate of banking, the encouragement of non-cash means of payment and the establishment of the necessary infrastructure for the remote spending of securities, the strengthening of the prerogatives of the Central Bank in the field of supervision of payment systems and means, the extension of the scope of application of the banking law in particular to offshore banks, remittance intermediation companies, micro-credit associations and Swiss Post financial services are all measures capable of consolidating the policy of preventing money laundering and terrorist financing. Nevertheless, with regard to one of the forms of transnational organized crime, an effective strategy to prevent and combat it requires sustained cooperation by our country with States and international institutions. In this regard, we should welcome all the initiatives already taken by Morocco in this field, in particular, the institutional twinning project carried out with the European Union and the assistance actions provided to our country in the form of study and training missions, organized by the United Nations, the International Monetary Fund, the FATF, the Arab Monetary Fund and the governments of several countries, in particular, Spain, France and the United States of America. I would also like to pay special tribute to all the ministerial departments concerned, in this case, the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of the Interior, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation and the Ministry of Economy and Finance, for their mobilization and the quality of their respective contributions throughout the process of drafting and adopting the law. I am convinced that the deep conviction of all the partners to work towards achieving the objectives assigned to this campaign is the best guarantee of the success of its work, which must be crowned by the formulation of recommendations likely to allow the appropriation of the preventive approach by all the subjects and to facilitate the application of the law. Finally, it is up to me to thank all those who have contributed to the material organization of this campaign and to conclude by soliciting media, audio-visual and written, to ensure adequate coverage, as they have done on the occasion of previous events aimed at strengthening the credibility of the cheque, promoting the use of the bank card and developing the partnership between banks and small and medium-sized enterprises. May God crown our work with success. Thank you.

De m<90>me, cette campagne vise la sensibilisation des diff<8e>rents acteurs concern<8e>s sur l<d5>importance de l<d5>approche pr<8e>ventive dans ce domaine et la mise en place de m<8e>canismes de communication entre les autorit<8e>s de supervision et de contr<99>le et les parties assujetties dans le cadre d<d5>une d<8e>marche de concertation r<8e>guli<8f>re. Je voudrais souligner, tout d<d5>abord, que le l<8e>gislateur a veill<8e> <88> ce que le dispositif l<8e>gal anti-blanchiment soit adapt<8e> au contexte national et assorti de toutes les garanties en mati<8f>re de pr<8e>servation du secret professionnel et de protection des personnes assujetties contre toutes poursuites judiciaires d<8e>coulant de l<d5>ex<8e>cution de leurs obligations. Ce dispositif qui s<d5>inscrit, <8e>galement, dans le cadre de la participation du Royaume <88> la mobilisation de la communaut<8e> internationale, en mati<8f>re de lutte contre la criminalit<8e> financi<8f>re organis<8e>e, int<8f>gre en droit interne les engagements internationaux pris par notre pays en vertu des conventions bilat<8e>rales et multilat<8e>rales qu<d5>il a ratifi<8e>es, les recommandations du GAFI et du Comit<8e> de B<89>le sur le devoir de vigilance <88> lgard de la client<8f>le ainsi que les dispositions pertinentes des r<8e>solutions du Conseil de S<8e>curit<8e>, bas<8e>es sur le chapitre VII de la Charte des Nations-Unies qui forment l<d5>un des piliers de l<d5>ordonnancement juridique international dans le domaine de la lutte contre le terrorisme. La lutte contre la criminalit<8e> financi<8f>re est au surplus devenue une composante essentielle dans les conventions de coop<8e>ration avec nos partenaires <8e>trangers, en particulier dans le cadre des accords de coop<8e>ration et de libre <8e>change conclus avec plusieurs pays. La conformit<8e> du dispositif national aux normes internationales en mati<8f>re de lutte contre le blanchiment de capitaux et le financement du terrorisme fait l<d5>objet dvaluation, selon une m<8e>thodologie uniforme appliqu<8e>e <88> tous les pays, de la part du Comit<8e> contre le Terrorisme relevant du Conseil de S<8e>curit<8e> des Nations-Unies et du Groupe d<d5>Action Financi<8f>re International pour le Moyen-Orient et l<d5>Afrique du Nord, constitu<8e> en 2004 et dont le Royaume du Maroc est l<d5>un des Etats fondateurs. Cette <8e>valuation constitue un <8e>l<8e>ment essentiel dans l<d5>appr<8e>ciation, faite par le Fonds Mon<8e>taire International et la Banque Mondiale, de la stabilit<8e> <8e>conomique et financi<8f>re et partant, influe sur la notation attribu<8e>e au Maroc par les agences sp<8e>cialis<8e>es. Compte tenu de tous ces <8e>l<8e>ments, il appara<94>t que la concertation sur la th<8e>matique de la lutte contre le blanchiment de capitaux et le financement du terrorisme rev<90>t une importance capitale pour l<d5>am<8e>lioration de l<d5>environnement des affaires dans notre pays, eu <8e>gard au r<99>le vital que peut jouer la pr<8e>vention de notre syst<8f>me <8e>conomico-financier contre toute utilisation <88> des fins illicites. MESDAMES ET MESSIEURS, Il est d<8e>sormais <8e>tabli que le blanchiment de capitaux a un effet hautement n<8e>gatif sur lconomie et le bien-<90>tre social d<d5>une nation. Il alt<8f>re les relations inter-entreprises, accro<94>t les risques des institutions financi<8f>res, nuit <88> la conduite de la politique <8e>conomique et financi<8f>re et porte une grave atteinte <88> la r<8e>putation du pays, en le rendant vuln<8e>rable au d<8e>veloppement d<d5>activit<8e>s criminelles. Cette forme de criminalit<8e> est d<d5>autant plus sournoise qu<d5>elle utilise souvent les soci<8e>t<8e>s de fa<8d>ade qui injectent ing<8e>nieusement les produits d<d5>activit<8e>s d<8e>lictueuses dans des circuits licites, pour masquer leur v<8e>ritable origine. Par ailleurs, le blanchiment favorise, d<d5>une part, les investissements de faible qualit<8e>, les activit<8e>s sp<8e>culatives et la volatilit<8e> des capitaux et renforce, d<d5>autre part, le pouvoir financier des d<8e>linquants, dans un environnement international marqu<8e> par la globalisation de lconomie et le caract<8f>re transnational des activit<8e>s criminelles qui empruntent des formes sans cesse mutantes dans des <8e>conomies de plus en plus financiaris<8e>es. Je voudrais ici, pour ma part, m<d5>arr<90>ter, de fa<8d>on particuli<8f>re, sur le secteur bancaire et financier national, relevant directement de la supervision et du contr<99>le de Bank Al-Maghrib, pour souligner que l<d5>int<8e>grit<8e> de ce secteur exige le respect de normes juridiques, professionnelles et d<8e>ontologiques rigoureuses et le renforcement de la confiance dans les institutions bancaires et financi<8f>res ainsi que la pr<8e>servation de leur image et de leur renom. Trois enjeux majeurs me paraissent devoir <90>tre relev<8e>s par ces institutions : - un enjeu culturel de sensibilisation, de formation et de mobilisation de leurs ressources humaines pour qu<d5>elles s<d5>approprient les nouveaux dispositifs et modes de comportement qu<d5>ils appellent ; - un enjeu technique dict<8e> par l<d5>adaptation des syst<8f>mes d<d5>information et la segmentation de la client<8f>le en fonction des risques ; - un enjeu d<d5>efficience li<8e> <88> l<d5>exigence d<d5>un syst<8f>me de reporting renforc<8e> et fiable. C<d5>est ainsi que Bank Al-Maghrib, dans le cadre de l<d5>exercice de ses missions statutaires, a anticip<8e> l<d5>entr<8e>e en vigueur de la loi anti.blanchiment, en initiant, en collaboration avec les organisations professionnelles, des actions visant, notamment, <88> renforcer les mesures prudentielles, <88> asseoir et <88> diffuser une v<8e>ritable culture de vigilance, de pr<8e>vention, de conformit<8e> et dthique. A cet <8e>gard, Bank Al-Maghrib a, d<8f>s d<8e>cembre 2003, fix<8e> les r<8f>gles minimales que les <8e>tablissements de cr<8e>dit sont tenus d<d5>observer au titre du devoir de vigilance au sujet de la client<8f>le. Ce devoir de vigilance a, d<d5>ailleurs, <8e>t<8e> consacr<8e>, par la suite, par l<d5>article 84 de la nouvelle loi bancaire, promulgu<8e>e le 14 f<8e>vrier 2006 et <8e>tendu <88> toute op<8e>ration dont la cause <8e>conomique ou le caract<8f>re licite n<d5>est pas apparent. Les dispositions de la loi bancaire ainsi que celles de la loi relative <88> la lutte contre le blanchiment de capitaux ont amen<8e> Bank Al-Maghrib <88> compl<8e>ter et <88> mettre <88> jour, en ao<9e>t 2007, la circulaire sur le dispositif de vigilance du 24 d<8e>cembre 2003, en pr<8e>voyant des r<8f>gles relatives au profilage de la client<8f>le en fonction du degr<8e> de risque, <88> la fixation de seuils au-del<88> desquels les op<8e>rations pourraient <90>tre consid<8e>r<8e>es comme inhabituelles ou suspectes et <88> l<d5>examen particulier de certaines op<8e>rations financi<8f>res r<8e>alis<8e>es par des interm<8e>diaires professionnels. Le champ d<d5>application de cette circulaire a <8e>t<8e> <8e>tendu aux organismes assimil<8e>s aux <8e>tablissements de cr<8e>dit. Aussi, avons-nous exig<8e> que ces institutions se dotent d<d5>une structure d<8e>di<8e>e <88> la gestion du dispositif interne de vigilance permettant d<d5>assurer la liaison avec l<d5>Unit<8e> de Traitement du Renseignement Financier, plac<8e>e aupr<8f>s de la Primature, et disposent d<d5>un syst<8f>me d<d5>information centralis<8e>, ad<8e>quat et performant. L<d5>efficacit<8e> de toutes ces mesures appelle n<8e>cessairement la mise en place, d<d5>une part, de programmes de formation et de sensibilisation du personnel des organismes assujettis et, d<d5>autre part, de la fonction de conformit<8e>. Nous avons ainsi compl<8e>t<8e> ce dispositif de vigilance par deux directives dat<8e>es du 31 ao<9e>t 2007. La premi<8f>re arr<90>te les principes pour l<d5>institution par les <8e>tablissements de cr<8e>dit de la fonction de conformit<8e> (compliance), en charge de la pr<8e>vention du risque de sanctions judiciaires, administratives ou disciplinaires, de pertes financi<8f>res ou d<d5>atteinte <88> la r<8e>putation cons<8e>cutivement au non-respect des dispositions l<8e>gales et r<8e>glementaires, et des normes et usages d<8e>ontologiques et professionnels propres <88> leur activit<8e>. La seconde relative <88> la gouvernance au sein des <8e>tablissements de cr<8e>dit, consiste en un r<8e>f<8e>rentiel de saines pratiques pour la mise en <cf>uvre par ces <8e>tablissements d<d5>un mode de gouvernance efficient. Ces mesures ont permis de bien pr<8e>parer le syst<8f>me bancaire <88> la mise en <cf>uvre de la loi anti-blanchiment, comme cela ressort de lvaluation par la Banque Centrale des dispositifs internes des banques. Les premiers r<8e>sultats de cette <8e>valuation sont globalement satisfaisants. Les banques ont institu<8e> la fonction de conformit<8e>, nomm<8e> ses responsables et leurs suppl<8e>ants, impl<8e>ment<8e> des progiciels param<8e>trables adapt<8e>s au traitement des op<8e>rations suspectes et au profilage de la client<8f>le et se sont dot<8e>es de moyens d<d5>analyse et de d<8e>tection afin d<d5>assumer leur obligation de d<8e>claration de soup<8d>on <88> l<d5>Unit<8e> de Traitement du Renseignement Financier. Bien entendu, il est imp<8e>ratif que ces dispositifs soient constamment adapt<8e>s et fassent l<d5>objet d<d5>une surveillance r<8e>guli<8f>re. Bank Al-Maghrib, en tant que personne assujettie, s<d5>est conform<8e>e elle-m<90>me aux nouvelles prescriptions l<8e>gales, en se dotant d<d5>un dispositif institutionnel, op<8e>rationnel et technique conforme aux meilleures pratiques des Banques Centrales en la mati<8f>re. MESDAMES ET MESSIEURS, L<d5>am<8e>lioration du taux de bancarisation, l<d5>encouragement des moyens de paiement scripturaux et la mise en place de l<d5>infrastructure n<8e>cessaire pour la t<8e>l<8e>compensation des valeurs, le renforcement des pr<8e>rogatives de la Banque Centrale dans le domaine de la surveillance des syst<8f>mes et moyens de paiement, l<d5>extension du champ d<d5>application de la loi bancaire en particulier aux banques offshore, aux entreprises d<d5>interm<8e>diation en mati<8f>re de transfert de fonds, aux associations de micro-cr<8e>dit et aux services financiers de la Poste, sont autant de mesures <88> m<90>me de consolider la politique de pr<8e>vention du blanchiment de capitaux et du financement du terrorisme. Il n<d5>en demeure pas moins que s<d5>agissant de l<d5>une des formes de criminalit<8e> transnationale organis<8e>e, une strat<8e>gie efficace de pr<8e>vention et de lutte en la mati<8f>re appelle une coop<8e>ration soutenue de notre pays avec les Etats et les Institutions Internationales. A cet <8e>gard, il convient de saluer toutes les initiatives d<8e>j<88> prises par le Maroc dans ce domaine, notamment, le projet de jumelage institutionnel men<8e> avec l<d5>Union europ<8e>enne et les actions d<d5>assistance fournies <88> notre pays sous forme de missions dtude et de formation, organis<8e>es par les Nations-Unies, le Fonds Mon<8e>taire International, le GAFI, le Fonds Mon<8e>taire Arabe et les gouvernements de plusieurs pays, notamment, l<d5>Espagne, la France et les Etats-Unis d<d5>Am<8e>rique. Je tiens, <8e>galement, <88> rendre un hommage particulier <88> tous les d<8e>partements minist<8e>riels concern<8e>s, en l<d5>occurrence, le Minist<8f>re de la Justice, le Minist<8f>re de l<d5>Int<8e>rieur, le Minist<8f>re des Affaires Etrang<8f>res et de la Coop<8e>ration et le Minist<8f>re de l<d5>Economie et des Finances, pour leur mobilisation et la qualit<8e> de leur contribution respective tout au long du processus dlaboration et d<d5>adoption de la loi. Je suis persuad<8e> que la conviction profonde de tous les partenaires d<d5><cf>uvrer <88> la r<8e>alisation des objectifs assign<8e>s <88> cette campagne, constitue la meilleure garantie du succ<8f>s de ses travaux, qui devront <90>tre couronn<8e>s par la formulation de recommandations de nature <88> permettre l<d5>appropriation de l<d5>approche pr<8e>ventive par l<d5>ensemble des assujettis et <88> faciliter l<d5>application de la loi. Il me revient, enfin, de remercier tous ceux qui ont contribu<8e> <88> l<d5>organisation mat<8e>rielle de la pr<8e>sente campagne et de conclure en sollicitant des m<8e>dias, audio-visuels et <8e>crits, de lui assurer une couverture ad<8e>quate, comme ils l<d5>ont fait <88> l<d5>occasion des pr<8e>c<8e>dentes manifestations visant le renforcement de la cr<8e>dibilit<8e> du ch<8f>que, la promotion de l<d5>utilisation de la carte bancaire et le d<8e>veloppement du partenariat banques/petites et moyennes entreprises. text: NATIONAL AWARENESS CAMPAIGN "For a better partnership Banks/Small and Medium Enterprises at the Service of Human Development" INAUGURAL ADDRESS BY MR. ABDELLATIF JOUAHRI GOVERNOR OF BANK AL-MAGHRIB A ra Thursday , 23 November 2006 Ministers; Distinguished Ambassadors; Presidents and Directors General; Ladies and gentlemen; It is a real pleasure for me to welcome you to the Bank Al-Maghrib training center for the launch of the national campaign on the financing of Small and Medium Enterprises. The theme of our meeting today is of particular importance to all of us: it is the beginning of a campaign but above all the hope of the completion of a project that should allow us to concretize all the current and future efforts to develop the financing and promotion of SMEs. The objective of this campaign is to loosen the structural constraints that hinder the activity of SMEs. To achieve this, it is essential to act together, in a spirit of openness and dialogue. The problem of SME financing has been the subject of several studies conducted by the Government, Bank Al-Maghrib and some national and international institutions. These different studies lead to convergent analyses on the nature and causes of the financing constraints weighing on Moroccan SMEs. First, they tend to show that the cost of bank credit to SMEs is relatively high, and that in addition these companies face difficulties in accessing credit that result in quantitative rationing. However, it is important to note that this issue is not specific to Morocco and is shared by most emerging countries. The high cost of credit to SMEs and the phenomenon of rationing are often explained by the existence of imperfections in the functioning of the credit market. These imperfections are generally linked to problems of transparency in the accounting of companies, difficulties in realizing the guarantees available to creditors and the unavailability of reliable and permanently updated information on the indebtedness and financial situation of borrowers. These imperfections in the credit market are a major challenge for the Central Bank, as the transmission of monetary policy effects is relatively slower and less effective for SMEs than for large companies. This weakness, it is important to stress, is explained by the structures of the credit market and does not depend directly on the stance of monetary policy. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN While Bank Al-Maghrib is closely interested in the financing conditions of smEs, this issue is also at the heart of the Government's actions. The public authorities have taken a series of initiatives to strengthen the financial resources dedicated to SMEs, by mobilizing lines of credit for them at concessional rates and by setting up guarantee funds, the latest of which is aimed at restructuring corporate debts. In addition, and with a view to making its action more efficient, the Government has put in place a multifaceted legal framework to support the creation and development of SMEs: in this regard, we can cite the SME Charter and the texts governing regional investment centres, free zones, micro-credit and venture capital. In addition, since its creation in 2002, the National Agency for Small and Medium Enterprises (ANPME) has proven to be an important instrument for the supervision and support of SMEs. The reflection continues: we have thus initiated for a few months already, in consultation with the Ministry of Finance, a study to examine the modalities of setting up a solid and sustainable national guarantee system and also intend to make an evaluation of the new provisions relating to venture capital. The problem of SME financing therefore calls for a global solution, which involves the commitment of several institutions, alongside the Government, within the framework of an organized and responsible consultation. Several recent experiences show that this method of approach can only be fruitful and effective. For example, the collaboration we have initiated with the Ministry of Justice and the Professional Group of Banks of Morocco (GPBM) on banking and judicial practices as well as on raising awareness of the problem of NSF cheques; as well as the joint work initiated with the GPBM and the Centre Monetique Interbancaire on bank cards; and more generally, on payment systems and means, have resulted in beneficial advances for the financial community. Our meeting today and the outreach campaign that will follow are therefore part of this logic of openness and enhanced dialogue. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN Bank Al-Maghrib's strategy to improve the functioning of the credit market for SMEs focuses on fostering the development of financial reporting. To achieve this fundamental objective, actions are being taken to encourage the pooling of financial information, the implementation of rating and scoring methodologies to improve the analysis of credit risk by banks, the standardization of accounting information and therefore the strengthening of creditor protection in order to facilitate relations between the SME and the banking sector. To pool the collection and dissemination of financial information, a partnership has been established between the Moroccan Office of Industrial and Commercial Property (OMPIC) and the Central Bank in order to optimize the use of the database available to this office. This will allow credit institutions to have access to reliable balance sheet information, and will open up the possibility for Bank Al-Maghrib to conduct more detailed sector studies, which would eventually be made available to companies. In this spirit, Bank Al-Maghrib has set up, as part of its internal organization, a department dedicated to relations with companies to ensure local actions and establish a lasting partnership with economic operators in the different regions of the Kingdom. Always in the spirit of improving the quality of financial reporting, Bank Al-Maghrib has embarked on a process of modernizing and strengthening the tools for collecting and sharing information on debtors' indebtedness and payment incidents to enable lending institutions to assess more objectively the risks incurred on their counterparties. Experience has shown that countries that have successful mechanisms in this area have a very high credit penetration rate and a significant reduction in defaults. In this context, Bank Al-Maghrib also asked banks to base their credit granting decisions on objective criteria, and to set the risk premium according to the profile of each company, based on a rating system. Thus, by means of a directive, we have laid down the minimum information elements to be required by credit institutions in the context of the examination of credit files, while requiring that financial documents be signed by the directors of the companies concerned and their reliability attested by professionals legally authorised for that purpose. In terms of bank-business relations, BAM was involved in facilitating the conclusion, in November 2005, of a partnership agreement by which banks undertake to support and assist companies in their development, in return for the commitment of SMEs to develop their activities within a framework of transparency. While I am pleased to welcome this initiative here, I also call on both parties to ensure the effective implementation of the clauses of this convention, which is likely to make it possible to overcome the main blocking factors often put forward. With regard to payment systems, we have undertaken, in close collaboration with the banking profession, several actions to comply with international standards. Thus, the Moroccan Gross Settlement System (SRBM), successfully launched last September, and the dematerialization of securities exchanged within the framework of the Moroccan Interbank System of Telecompensation (SIMT), which will be generalized to all regions of the Kingdom in 2007, should induce a more significant reduction in the time taken to settle values and transaction costs for the benefit of all banking customers. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN It is encouraging to note that the efforts made by the various stakeholders involved in supporting SMEs are beginning to bear fruit, whether in terms of the financing and guarantee funds set up or the action of the ANPME. Similarly, BAM's recent quarterly survey of banks on lending rates indicates that the easing of interest rates in the market is increasingly benefiting SMEs. In addition, banks that consider the SME sector to be a strategic vector for their development are working to adapt their internal organisation to meet the specific needs of these companies. I would like to take this opportunity to dispel some of the concerns that have been expressed about the impact of Basel II on SME financing. It should be noted, in that regard, that Bank Al-Maghrib has, within the framework of the 'national discretions' provided for in the Basel II framework, taken the decision to reduce the capital requirements to be set up by banks to cover the risks incurred on that category of undertaking. For their part, representatives of the SME sector are increasingly sensitive to the issue of financial transparency, as highlighted at the last SME conference. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN The results achieved so far, although they fall short of our expectations, reinforce our actions and encourage us to persevere with a view to their consolidation. This campaign will take place under the theme "For a better partnership between banks / Small and Medium Enterprises for human development" and will concern 7 regions of Morocco. The choice of this theme reflects the commitment of all the partners present here to place their action within the framework of the National Initiative for Human Development (INDH), and to make their contribution to the achievement of the objectives assigned to this Royal Initiative which aims at social promotion through economic development. In this context, particular attention should also be paid to the segment of unbanked SMEs and our combined efforts to put in place appropriate arrangements that take into account the informal environment in which they operate. The same interest should also be devoted to the supervision of the activity of the microcredit sector. This proximity campaign therefore aims to broaden the framework of our consultation in order to refine our diagnosis on the complex problem of SME financing at the global, sectoral or regional level, to formulate recommendations likely to strengthen the development of trust between the various stakeholders, and to promote the emergence of sustainable and consensual solutions. I cannot conclude without thanking the representatives of the partner countries, cooperation organisations and international financial institutions, most of whom are present here, for all the support they give to our actions in favour of SMEs, and remain convinced of their willingness to continue to accompany us in the future stages.

text: CONFERENCE UNDER THE THEME "Challenges and operating methods of the delegation of the Central Risks of Bank AL-Maghrib" INAUGURAL ADDRESS BY MR. GOVERNOR DE BANK AL-MAGHRIB Rabat Monday November 26th , 2007 Mr. Secretary General; Presidents and Directors General; Ladies and gentlemen ; It is a real pleasure for me to welcome you for this study day dedicated to the delegation of the Bank Al-Maghrib Risk Centre. The theme of this meeting is of particular importance: it is the beginning of the realization of a structuring project that should lead us to a global pooling of credit information in Morocco. The challenge for us is to build, in the long term, an integrated financial information system that meets the best standards in this area. To this end, Bank Al-Maghrib has embarked on a process of modernizing the tools for collecting and sharing information on credit and payment incidents related to the check. A partnership was also established in 2007 with the Moroccan Office of Industrial and Commercial Property (OMPIC) allowing us to exploit the database available to this office in order to conduct more detailed sectoral studies. In this spirit, Bank Al-Maghrib reorganized in 2007, the Department in charge of information centers by field of activity (data supply, application management and processing of requests for information from customers) in order to ensure efficient management of operations, to allow a permanent reliability of the information received and to offer quality services to the users of our plants. The objective of this study day is therefore: -to explain the challenges of the implementation of the delegation of the Bank Al-Maghrib risk centre, as well as the institutional and operational framework of the adopted model, -to share international experiences in the field of credit information -and to allow our partner Experian Holding France to present the services on which it has committed as part of this delegation. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN One of the main axes of Bank Al-Maghrib's strategy for improving the functioning of the credit market is the development of financial information. The difficulties in accessing credit are largely explained by the unavailability of reliable and up-to-date information on the financial situation of borrowers and their level of indebtedness. In this regard, the evaluation of information-sharing mechanisms has been the subject of several analyses since 2004 conducted by Bank Al-Maghrib in collaboration with certain institutions, both national and international. These arrangements were presented to most of the participants present here at the conference organized in May 2005 by Bank AL-Maghrib in collaboration with the International Finance Corporation and whose main recommendation was the need to implement a culture of credit information sharing. Experience has also shown that countries with Credit Bureaux have addressed the problem of "information asymmetry" and substantially improved the quality of their credit portfolios. The instruments developed by these Credit Bureaux contribute significantly to the accurate assessment of the creditworthiness of borrowers. In this context and following an international call for tenders, the Central Bank has delegated, as of September 21, 2007, and in accordance with the provisions of the new banking law, the management of its Central Risk Service to Experian Holding France, one of the international Credit Bureaux that have developed a convincing know-how in the field. The legal and technical conditions that governed this delegation also scrupulously respected the provisions of the Law on Delegated Management, including:  guaranteeing the principle of continuity of the public service and equal treatment of all users  and the obligation for the Credit Bureau to comply with the rules of good governance and confidentiality. For example, Bank Al-Maghrib issued circulars in April 2007:  the information that the institutions subject to tax must communicate to it for the proper functioning of the Risk Centralisation Service,  the terms and conditions of access to information held by the Credit Bureau  as well as the rights and obligations of all stakeholders (Credit Bureau, credit institutions and customers) formalized in a code of conduct. Compared to the current situation, this important project led by the Central Bank aims to: - to strengthen and modernize the existing infrastructure through the globalization of information, regardless of the amount and type of credit granted, - to know precisely the payment habits of customers, - to reduce outstanding debts, - increase the rate of access to bank financing while contributing to the lower cost of credit -and to protect the rights of borrowers. The Credit Bureau thus provides credit institutions with a reliable system allowing them to base their decisions on objective criteria, and to set the risk premium according to customer profiles through the production of credit reports and scoring. Therefore, I remain convinced that the establishment of such a system will be a catalyst for the development of credit, particularly for small and medium-sized enterprises and will contribute to the reduction of household over-indebtedness. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN Bank Al-Maghrib remains very aware that the security and confidentiality of the information managed by the Credit Bureau are elements of high sensitivity and constitute one of the main orientations of the project. To this end, Bank Al-Maghrib will ensure that adequate procedures and controls are in place to ensure the availability, integrity and security of information. In addition, it has all the legal and regulatory means empowering it to ensure, on a permanent basis, the smooth running of the delegated service and compliance with the rules applicable to it. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN The establishment of a Credit Bureau requires a lasting commitment on the part of all the stakeholders of the system and particularly the institutions subject to the system, which are both data providers and users of the services offered. The key to the success of such a system lies in the permanence of the quality of the data received, which conditions the return of reliable information reflecting at all times the real situation of borrowers. Also, the opportunity is given to me to sensitize credit institutions and microcredit associations on the need to fully adhere to this project and to undertake the necessary efforts to upgrade all their services concerned and also their information systems. Bank Al-Maghrib has also embarked on a process of modernization of its technological platform, as part of the redesign of its information centers, in order to respond efficiently to the needs of the new system, through an evolutionary technical base allowing the integration of current information centers and those programmed in the long term (central incidents on effects and general file of bank accounts). For its part, the Credit Bureau will ensure, in accordance with its commitments:  the establishment of a state-of-the-art technical infrastructure,  the development at the local level of know-how in line with international practices  and the production of powerful decision support tools for credit risk analysis. The active participation of all the actors concerned is therefore essential for the implementation of this important project, which is scheduled to be put into operational operation in the third quarter of 2008. LADIES AND GENTLEMEN By focusing on consultation, Bank Al-Maghrib has carried out in recent years with the banking and financial sector several structuring projects whose successful outcome has been recognized by international bodies. I remain convinced that this project will also have the same outcome knowing that Morocco is one of the first countries in the MENA region to set up a Credit Bureau. I would also like to stress that our compliance with international standards for the sharing of financial information will have a positive impact on the rating assigned to Morocco by specialised agencies. Finally, allow me to express my warmest thanks to all the speakers who have kindly responded to our invitation, and to the International Finance Corporation for its collaboration in this project and its participation in the organization of this conference. I cannot conclude without thanking the representatives of partner countries and regional and international financial institutions present here for all the support they have given to our actions to improve financial information sharing mechanisms, and remain confident in their willingness to continue to accompany us in the next steps.
